Japp then produced the charred fragment of paper recovered from the grate, and this, with the discovery of the beard in the attic, completed his evidence. But Sir Ernest’s cross-examination was yet to come. “What day was it when you searched the prisoner’s room?” “Tuesday, the 24th of July.” “Exactly a week after the tragedy?” “Yes.” “You found these two objects, you say, in the chest of drawers. Was the drawer unlocked?” “Yes.” “Does it not strike you as unlikely that a man who had committed a crime should keep the evidence of it in an unlocked drawer for anyone to find?” “He might have stowed them there in a hurry.” “But you have just said it was a whole week since the crime.
